question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

When I was in high school / I participated in several extracurricular activities / such as the debate team and the school newspaper / which help me developed my communication and writing skills.
option_1: When I was in high school
option_2: which help me developed my communication and writing skills
option_3: such as the debate team and the school newspaper
option_4: I participated in several extracurricular activities
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. which help me developed my communication and writing skills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The whole sentence is in the past tense ("When I was in high school", "I participated"). The relative clause must therefore use the past form "helped", not the present "help".

• A second error follows immediately: after the verb "help", English uses the pattern "help + object + (to) + V1" — i.e. "help me develop", never "help me developed".

◦ Correct: ... which helped me develop my communication and writing skills.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "When I was in high school" — a correct adverbial clause of time in the past tense.

• Option 3 "such as the debate team and the school newspaper" — "such as" correctly introduces examples.

• Option 4 "I participated in several extracurricular activities" — "participate in" is the right collocation and "participated" agrees with the past-tense frame.

NOTE

• Verbs of permission/causation take the bare infinitive: help / make / let / see / hear + object + V1 (He made me laugh; She let him go; They helped us carry the bags). "Help" alone also allows the to-infinitive: "helped me to develop".

• Rule of sequence of tenses: when the principal clause is in the past, the subordinate clause is normally also in the past.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The rise in temperature is playing havoc with India’s rainfall which is pertinent for India’s agriculture sector.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. rainfall which is significant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pertinent" means relevant to / connected with a particular matter. (प्रासंगिक) It is used for remarks, questions and information — "a pertinent question", "pertinent facts".

• The sense required here is that rainfall is very important / crucial for agriculture, and the word that carries that meaning is "significant" (महत्वपूर्ण).

◦ Correct: The rise in temperature is playing havoc with India's rainfall which is significant for India's agriculture sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rainfall who is pertinent" — "who" is used only for persons; for a thing such as "rainfall" the relative pronoun must be "which". Grammatically wrong.

• Option 3 "decant" is a verb meaning to pour liquid gently from one container to another; it cannot follow "is" as an adjective and makes no sense here.

• Option 4 "mendicant" means a beggar; one who lives on alms (भिखारी / भिक्षुक) — completely unrelated, and "was" also breaks the present-tense frame.

NOTE

• Idiom used in the sentence: "to play havoc with" = to damage or disturb something badly (तबाही मचाना).

• Synonyms of significant: important, momentous, notable, consequential, vital. Antonyms: trivial, insignificant, negligible.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Sameera has been in ________ since she got selected for a highly paid job at a multinational company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. seventh heaven.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to be in seventh heaven" means to be extremely happy; in a state of great joy or bliss. (अत्यंत प्रसन्न होना / फूले न समाना)

• Getting selected for a highly paid job in an MNC is a cause of great delight, so the blank needs an idiom of extreme happiness.

◦ Correct: Sameera has been in seventh heaven since she got selected for a highly paid job at a multinational company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "all the rage" = very fashionable/popular at a particular time (Baggy jeans are all the rage this season).

• Option 3 "in the dark" = kept uninformed / ignorant about something (They kept the staff in the dark about the merger).

• Option 4 "a cold day in July" (also "when hell freezes over") = something that will never happen.

NOTE

• Other idioms for great happiness: "on cloud nine", "over the moon", "walking on air", "on top of the world", "jump for joy".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I hope you break a leg at your performance tonight!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Perform well.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Break a leg" is a theatrical idiom used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance on stage. It means do well / perform brilliantly. (शुभकामनाएँ देना)

◦ Example: "Break a leg!" the director told the actors before the curtain rose.

• The clue in the sentence is "I hope you ... at your performance tonight" — a wish of good luck, not of injury.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Hurt yourself" is the literal meaning of the words, which is exactly what an idiom does not mean. Superstitious theatre people avoided saying "good luck" directly, so they said the opposite.

• Options 1 "Give up" and 2 "Make a mistake" have no connection with the idiom.

NOTE

• Other performance/luck idioms: "knock 'em dead" (impress the audience), "bring the house down" (win huge applause), "steal the show" (attract all the attention), "fingers crossed" (hoping for luck).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Winning the championship was a dream come true for the team, but being awarded the MVP trophy was ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the icing on the cake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The icing on the cake" means an extra good thing that makes an already good situation even better. (सोने पे सुहागा)

• Here, winning the championship was already excellent; the MVP trophy is an additional bonus on top of it — exactly the sense of the idiom.

◦ Correct: ... but being awarded the MVP trophy was the icing on the cake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a silver lining" = a hopeful or comforting aspect of an otherwise bad situation ("Every cloud has a silver lining"). The situation here is not bad at all.

• Option 2 "a bird in the bush" comes from "A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush" and refers to something uncertain/not yet obtained.

• Option 3 "cold turkey" = to stop an addiction abruptly and completely (He quit smoking cold turkey).

NOTE

• Similar idioms of an added bonus: "a cherry on top", "a feather in one's cap" (an achievement to be proud of), "the cream on top".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

We requested grandmother to extend her visit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Curtail.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extend" here means to make something last longer; to prolong. (बढ़ाना / लंबा करना)

• Its antonym is "Curtail", which means to cut short, reduce or restrict. (कम करना / छोटा करना)

◦ Example: Heavy rain forced them to curtail the trip, though they had planned to extend it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Imperil" = to put in danger; endanger (संकट में डालना).

• Option 3 "Assail" = to attack violently; to criticise fiercely (हमला करना).

• Option 4 "Bewail" = to express great sorrow or regret over something (विलाप करना).

NOTE

• Synonyms of extend: prolong, lengthen, protract, expand, stretch. Antonyms: curtail, shorten, abridge, truncate, reduce.

• Note the family of "-ail" verbs often tested by SSC: assail (attack), bewail (lament), curtail (cut short), avail (make use of), prevail (win/be widespread).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Simon is afraid of closed space.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has claustrophobia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Claustrophobia" is an extreme or irrational fear of confined/closed spaces such as lifts, tunnels and small rooms. (संवृतिभीति / बंद जगह का डर)

◦ Correct: Simon has claustrophobia.

• The one-word substitution is exactly what the question asks for, so the whole underlined segment "is afraid of closed space" is replaced.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Xenophobia" = fear or hatred of foreigners/strangers.

• Option 2 "Ecophobia" = fear of the home/household surroundings (also used for fear of ecological problems).

• Option 4 "Hydrophobia" = fear of water (also another name for rabies).

NOTE

• Other phobias frequently asked in SSC exams: Acrophobia (heights), Agoraphobia (open/public places), Nyctophobia (darkness), Arachnophobia (spiders), Pyrophobia (fire), Zoophobia (animals), Ophidiophobia (snakes), Thanatophobia (death).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Magnificent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Glorious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Magnificent" (adjective) means extremely beautiful, grand, impressive or splendid. (शानदार / भव्य)

• "Glorious" also means splendid, magnificent, deserving great praise, so it is the closest synonym.

◦ Example: The Taj Mahal is a magnificent / glorious monument of Mughal architecture.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Justify" is a verb meaning to show that something is right or reasonable — wrong part of speech and wrong sense.

• Option 3 "Highest" refers to physical height or rank, not to grandeur or splendour.

• Option 4 "Modest" (simple, humble, not showy) is an antonym of magnificent.

NOTE

• Synonyms of magnificent: splendid, majestic, grand, superb, sublime, imposing, resplendent. Antonyms: modest, ordinary, humble, shabby, unimpressive.

question:
The sentence given below contains some spelling errors. Select the option that has the correct spellings.

Appliications of subjects like Physiks and chemmistry in our dayly life also have higher visibelity than those of Biology.
option_1: Applicasions of subjects like Physiks and Cemistry in our dayly life also have higher visibility than those of Biology.
option_2: Appliications of subjects like Physics and chemistry in our dayly life also have higher visibelity than those of Biology.
option_3: Applications of subjects like Physics and Chemistry in our daily life also have higher visibility than those of Biology.
option_4: Applicacions of subjects like Physics and chemmistry in our daily life also have higher visibilety than those of Biology.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Applications of subjects like Physics and Chemistry in our daily life also have higher visibility than those of Biology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence contains five misspelt words. The correct forms are:

◦ "Appliications" → Applications (APP + LI + CA + TIONS)

◦ "Physiks" → Physics

◦ "chemmistry" → Chemistry (single "m")

◦ "dayly" → daily (DAI + LY)

◦ "visibelity" → visibility (VIS + I + BIL + ITY)

• Only Option 3 corrects all five words at once.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 still keeps the wrong "Applicasions", "Physiks" and "Cemistry" and "dayly".

• Option 2 still keeps "Appliications", "dayly" and "visibelity".

• Option 4 still keeps "Applicacions", "chemmistry" and "visibilety".

NOTE

• The noun-forming suffix is spelt "-tion" (application, education, information), never "-sion" after "ca-", and never "-cion".

• Adjectives in "-ible" form nouns in "-ibility": visible → visibility, possible → possibility, responsible → responsibility. Adjectives in "-able" give "-ability": capable → capability.

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The weather is cold tonight than it was yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. colder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The conjunction "than" is a marker of the comparative degree. Whenever "than" is used for comparison, the adjective before it must be in the comparative form.

• "Cold" is a short (one-syllable) adjective, so its comparative is formed by adding -er: cold → colder → coldest.

◦ Correct: The weather is colder tonight than it was yesterday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "its" — "The weather its cold" is ungrammatical; "is" (the verb) is correct and must not be replaced by the possessive "its".

• Option 2 "are" — "weather" is an uncountable singular noun and takes the singular verb "is".

• Option 3 "were" — the pronoun "it" is singular, so "it was" is correct; "it were" is wrong here.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: one-syllable and some two-syllable adjectives take -er / -est (cold–colder–coldest, happy–happier–happiest); longer adjectives take more / most (beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful). Never use "more" with "-er" (× more colder).

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error in the given sentence.

Little children are afraid to go to school because of the agrassive seniors who tend to bully them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Aggressive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Aggressive" — behaving in an angry, forceful or threatening way; ready to attack. (आक्रामक)

• Spelling key: AG + GRES + SIVE — a double "g" and a double "s".

◦ Correct: Little children are afraid to go to school because of the aggressive seniors who tend to bully them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Aggresive" — only one "s"; wrong.

• Option 3 "Agrresive" and Option 4 "Agrressive" — the double letter has been wrongly put on "r"; wrong.

NOTE

• Related words: aggression (noun), aggressively (adverb), aggressor (the one who attacks first).

• Similar double-consonant traps: occurrence, embarrassment, accommodation, possession, recommend, necessary, harassment.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The scratches on her hands were clear signs of domestic violence, ______ and said that she got scratched by barbed wire fencing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. yet she lied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The words after the blank — "and said that she got scratched by barbed wire fencing" — need a subject + finite verb before them so that the two verbs ("lied ... and said") can be joined by "and".

• The sense of the sentence is one of contrast: the scratches clearly proved domestic violence, but in spite of that she gave a false explanation. The contrastive conjunction "yet" carries exactly this meaning.

◦ Correct: The scratches on her hands were clear signs of domestic violence, yet she lied and said that she got scratched by barbed wire fencing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "and poverty" supplies a noun, leaving "and said" without a subject.

• Option 3 "which was enough evidence" gives a relative clause, again leaving "and said" without a subject and losing the contrast.

• Option 4 "done a while ago" is a participial phrase with no subject or finite verb.

NOTE

• Conjunctions of contrast: but, yet, still, however, nevertheless, whereas, although/though. Note that "although" and "yet/but" are never used together in the same clause in modern English.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rahul’s sister says that my brother is the best dancer in the city.
option_1: her brother is the best dancer in the city
option_2: my brother was the best dancer in the city
option_3: her brother was the best dancer in the city
option_4: his brother was the best dancer in the city
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. her brother is the best dancer in the city.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a sentence of indirect (reported) speech. In reported speech the pronouns must change according to the person of the reporter.

• The speaker is "Rahul's sister" (a female, third person), so the first-person possessive "my" must become the third-person feminine possessive "her".

• The reporting verb "says" is in the present tense; when the reporting verb is in the present, the tense of the reported clause does not change. So "is" must remain "is", not become "was".

◦ Correct: Rahul's sister says that her brother is the best dancer in the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 keeps the wrong pronoun "my" and also wrongly back-shifts the verb.

• Option 3 has the right pronoun "her" but wrongly changes "is" to "was".

• Option 4 uses "his", which would refer to some male, not to Rahul's sister.

NOTE

• Golden rule of narration: back-shifting of tense happens only when the reporting verb is in the past (said, told, asked). With "says / say / will say / has said", the reported speech keeps its original tense.

• A universal truth or habitual fact also stays in the present even after a past reporting verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’.

A wonder in the plant kingdom, the Great Banyan Tree of the AJC Bose Botanical Garden at Shibpur in Howrah, occupies a unique position in the world records.
option_4: being occupied a unique position of
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No improvement required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "occupies a unique position in" is already perfectly correct:

◦ The subject "the Great Banyan Tree" is singular, so the singular verb "occupies" is right.

◦ The article before "unique" must be "a", not "an", because "unique" begins with the consonant sound /juː/ ("yoo-neek"). The choice of a/an depends on sound, not on the letter.

◦ The preposition "in" correctly collocates with "a position in the world records".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "occupying" is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a finite verb.

• Option 2 "an unique" is a classic article error — always "a unique", "a university", "a European", "a one-rupee coin".

• Option 4 "being occupied a unique position of" is an ungrammatical passive with a wrong preposition.

NOTE

• Static-GK bonus: the Great Banyan Tree stands in the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden, Shibpur, Howrah (West Bengal). It is over 250 years old and covers about 1.5 hectares, making it one of the widest tree canopies in the world.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The cholera is a frightful disease.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The cholera.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of diseases are uncountable nouns and do not take the definite article "the". We say cholera, malaria, cancer, diabetes, typhoid, AIDS — not "the cholera", "the malaria".

◦ Correct: Cholera is a frightful disease.

• Hence the segment "The cholera" carries the error and the article "the" must be dropped.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "is" is correct — "cholera" is singular/uncountable.

• Option 3 "frightful disease" is correct — "frightful" (terrible, dreadful) properly qualifies "disease".

• Option 4 "a" is correct — "a frightful disease" needs the indefinite article before a singular countable noun.

NOTE

• Exceptions to the rule: a few disease names do take "the" — "the flu", "the measles", "the mumps", "the plague", "the chickenpox" (informally).

• Articles are also omitted before names of meals (breakfast, lunch), languages (Hindi, English), subjects (Physics), and most proper nouns.

• Static GK: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, spread through contaminated water and food; treatment relies on ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution).

question:
The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors.

Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to preceede my knowledge of things other than me.
option_1: Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to preceede my knowledge of things other then me.
option_2: Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to precede my knowledge of things other than me.
option_3: Knowlegde and awareness about my own self has to preceede my knowlegde of things other than me.
option_4: Knowledge and awarenes about my own self has to preceede my knowledge of things other than me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to precede my knowledge of things other than me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word in the given sentence is "preceede". The correct spelling is "precede" — to come or go before something in time or order. (पहले आना)

• Spelling key: PRE + CEDE (only one "e" in the second part).

• Option 2 is the only choice in which every word is correctly spelt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps "preceede" and also wrongly uses "then" for "than" (than = comparison; then = time).

• Option 3 misspells "Knowledge" twice as "Knowlegde" and keeps "preceede".

• Option 4 misspells "awareness" as "awarenes" and keeps "preceede".

NOTE

• Confusables: precede (to go before) vs proceed (to go forward/continue) vs supersede (to replace). Only three English verbs end in "-ceed": exceed, proceed, succeed; the rest use "-cede" (concede, recede, secede, intercede, precede).

• "Precedent" (a previous example) and "unprecedented" (never done before) come from the same root.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

If Peter said he would get that book for you, he will do it. He always ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. keeps his word.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to keep one's word" means to do what one has promised; to honour a promise. (अपना वादा निभाना)

• The context — "If Peter said he would get that book for you, he will do it" — states that Peter is reliable, which is exactly the sense of keeping one's word.

◦ Correct: He always keeps his word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "keep something under one's hat" = to keep it secret.

• Option 2 "keep someone at arm's length" = to avoid becoming too friendly or involved with someone.

• Option 4 "keep your shirt on" = stay calm; don't lose your temper.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "a man of his word" (a dependable person), "go back on one's word" (to break a promise), "give one's word" (to promise), "as good as one's word" (does exactly what he promised).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It has raining very hard and he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. is raining.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "has raining" is ungrammatical: after "has" we need either a past participle ("has rained") or "been + V-ing" ("has been raining"). Neither is offered.

• The second half of the sentence is in the simple present ("he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops"), showing that the action is happening now. The tense that expresses an action going on at the moment of speaking is the present continuous: is + V-ing.

◦ Correct: It is raining very hard and he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "shall rain" is future tense and does not match "he has ... umbrella" (present).

• Option 3 "will be rainy" is also future and changes the structure awkwardly.

• Option 4 "rained" is simple past and clashes with the present-tense second clause.

NOTE

• Present continuous = is/am/are + V-ing; used for (i) actions happening now, (ii) temporary actions, (iii) fixed near-future plans.

• With the dummy subject "It" for weather, we say: It is raining / It is snowing / It is getting dark.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Shiya had more grit than her other siblings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. courage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Grit" (noun) means courage, determination and strength of character; the ability to keep going in the face of difficulty. (साहस / दृढ़ता)

◦ Example: It takes real grit to finish a marathon after an injury.

• Hence "courage" is the closest synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "power" refers to physical strength or authority, not to determination in adversity.

• Option 2 "level" (a standard/height) and Option 3 "gap" (an empty space) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of grit: courage, fortitude, tenacity, mettle, pluck, resolve, backbone, spine. Antonyms: cowardice, timidity, faint-heartedness.

• "Grit" also literally means small particles of stone or sand; the figurative meaning of courage grows out of the idea of toughness.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) The twins are / (B) often told that / (C) they are resembling / (D) each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Resemble" is a stative verb (a verb of state, not of action). Stative verbs are not used in the continuous (V-ing) form.

• Therefore "they are resembling" is wrong; it must be the simple present "they resemble".

◦ Correct: The twins are often told that they resemble each other.

• Note also that "resemble" is a transitive verb that takes a direct object without any preposition — "resemble each other", never "resemble with/to each other".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "The twins are" — correct plural subject-verb agreement.

• Part (B) "often told that" — correct passive structure with the adverb of frequency in its usual mid-position.

• Part (D) "each other" — correctly used as the reciprocal pronoun for two persons.

NOTE

• Common stative verbs never used in the continuous form: know, believe, understand, resemble, belong, own, possess, contain, consist, seem, prefer, hate, love, want, need, mean, hear, see, smell.

• Reciprocal pronouns: "each other" for two; "one another" for more than two.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb required here is "to set off (something) against", which means to make something stand out clearly by contrast with its background. (उभारकर दिखाना)

◦ Correct: Each essay is set off against its background ...

• The clue is the word "against its background" — a thing is always set off against a background so that it becomes prominent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "set in" = (of weather, a season, an infection) to begin and be likely to continue — "The monsoon has set in".

• Option 2 "set at" is not a standard phrasal verb in this sense.

• Option 3 "set on" = to attack ("The dogs were set on the intruder").

NOTE

• Other meanings of "set off": (i) to start a journey ("We set off at dawn"), (ii) to cause something to explode or begin ("The spark set off a fire", "It set off an alarm").

• Related phrasal verbs with "set": set up (establish), set aside (keep for later), set back (delay), set out (begin a journey/explain in detail), set about (start doing).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. its.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes before the noun phrase "summary and critical commentary" and must show whose summary it is — that is, the summary of each essay. The word needed is therefore a possessive adjective.

• "Its" is the possessive adjective of the pronoun "it" and refers back to "Each essay" mentioned at the beginning of the sentence.

◦ Correct: ... made simpler by providing its summary and critical commentary ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "there" is an adverb of place / an introductory word and cannot modify a noun.

• Options 3 "that" and 4 "this" are demonstratives; used here they would point to something specific and previously named, which does not suit "providing ___ summary".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "its" (possessive adjective — the dog wagged its tail) with "it's" (contraction of it is / it has). The possessive "its" never takes an apostrophe.

• Possessive adjectives: my, our, your, his, her, its, their.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. discussions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is part of a list of academic features the book provides: "summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and ______ of important critical and theoretical issues".

• The word must be a plural noun that collocates with "of ... issues" in an academic sense. "Discussions of important critical and theoretical issues" is the natural, standard academic expression.

◦ Correct: ... short notes on textual issues, and discussions of important critical and theoretical issues ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mindset" (a fixed attitude) is singular and does not take "of ... issues".

• Option 2 "chats" is far too informal for an academic textbook context.

• Option 4 "thinking" is uncountable and abstract; "thinking of important issues" does not convey the sense of a written treatment.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always check three things: (i) the grammatical form required (noun/verb/adjective, singular/plural), (ii) the collocation with the following preposition, and (iii) the register (formal vs informal) of the passage.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. glossary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "glossary" is an alphabetical list of difficult or technical terms with their explanations, usually given at the end of a book. (शब्दावली)

• The sentence itself defines it: "______ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference" — the mention of terms, at the end and ready reference points unmistakably to a glossary.

• Note also the singular verb "is" after the blank, which requires a singular noun — "glossary" is singular, while "figures" and "data" are plural.

◦ Correct: Glossary of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "figures" (illustrations/numbers) and Option 4 "data" (facts and statistics) are plural and do not explain terms.

• Option 3 "grammar" is the system of rules of a language, not a list of terms.

NOTE

• Parts of a book: preface/foreword (introductory note), table of contents (list of chapters), appendix (extra material), bibliography (list of sources), glossary (list of terms), index (alphabetical list of topics with page numbers) — all favourite SSC vocabulary items.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. needs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "cater" means to provide what is required or wanted by a particular group of people. Its standard collocation is "cater to / for the needs of". (आवश्यकताओं की पूर्ति करना)

• A textbook serves the academic requirements of students and teachers, so "needs" is the only appropriate noun.

◦ Correct: This book will cater the needs of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "desires" and Option 3 "feelings" refer to personal wishes and emotions, not to academic requirements.

• Option 2 "whims" means sudden, unreasonable ideas or fancies — clearly negative and unsuitable for a textbook's purpose.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "needs": meet the needs, fulfil the needs, cater to the needs, address the needs, suit the needs.

• "Cater" is normally followed by to (American/Indian usage) or for (British usage): "The hotel caters for/to vegetarians".

question: Which of the following Indian playback singers received the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), affectionately called the "Nightingale of India" (स्वर कोकिला), was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian award.

• She was only the second singer/musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, after the shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001) — both were honoured the same year.

• She recorded songs in over 36 Indian languages across a career spanning more than seven decades, and famously sang "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon" in 1963.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other awards of Lata Mangeshkar: Padma Bhushan (1969), Padma Vibhushan (1999), Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989) and the Legion of Honour (France's highest civilian honour, 2007).

• KS Chithra — the "Nightingale of South India", a Padma Bhushan awardee and a six-time National Film Award winner.

• Geeta Dutt — a celebrated playback singer of the 1950s, known for songs in Pyaasa and Kaagaz Ke Phool.

• Asha Bhosle — Lata's younger sister; she received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2000) and the Padma Vibhushan (2008), but not the Bharat Ratna.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954. Musicians honoured with it include MS Subbulakshmi (1998), Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001), Pandit Ravi Shankar (1999), Bhupen Hazarika (2019, posthumous) and Lata Mangeshkar (2001).

question: Which of the following cricket players wrote the autobiography ‘Playing It My Way’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sachin Tendulkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Playing It My Way" (2014) is the autobiography of Sachin Tendulkar, co-written with Boria Majumdar. It was released soon after his retirement from international cricket in November 2013.

• Sachin Tendulkar, the "Master Blaster"/"God of Cricket", holds the records of 100 international centuries and more than 34,000 international runs, and was the first batter to score a double century in a men's ODI (200 not out vs South Africa, Gwalior, 2010).

• He received the Bharat Ratna in 2014, becoming the first sportsperson to be so honoured.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Yuvraj Singh — autobiography "The Test of My Life" (his fight against cancer); famous for six sixes in an over against Stuart Broad in the 2007 T20 World Cup.

• Sourav Ganguly — "A Century Is Not Enough"; former India captain and BCCI President (2019–2022).

• Kiran More — former wicketkeeper and chairman of selectors; his book is "No Boundaries".

NOTE

• Other cricket autobiographies often asked: "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "The Race of My Life" (Milkha Singh, athletics), "Unbreakable" (Mary Kom, boxing), "Ace Against Odds" (Sania Mirza, tennis), "Sunny Days" (Sunil Gavaskar).

question: In which city is the India Gate situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India Gate stands on Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath) in New Delhi. It is a 42-metre (about 138 ft) high war memorial arch.

• It was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1931. Originally called the All India War Memorial, it commemorates about 84,000 Indian soldiers who died in the First World War (1914–21) and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

• The names of over 13,000 servicemen are inscribed on its walls.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Amar Jawan Jyoti, installed in 1972 after the 1971 India-Pakistan war, burned beneath the arch until January 2022, when its flame was merged with the flame at the National War Memorial nearby.

• In September 2022, a statue of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was unveiled under the canopy behind India Gate (the canopy earlier held a statue of King George V).

NOTE

• Other landmarks by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker in New Delhi: Rashtrapati Bhavan (earlier Viceroy's House), North and South Block, and the Parliament House (Baker).

• Famous gates: Gateway of India — Mumbai; Buland Darwaza — Fatehpur Sikri; Charminar — Hyderabad.

question: Who authored the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ in 1901, which was highly critical of the economic impact of British Rule?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901) was written by Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the "Grand Old Man of India" (भारत के वयोवृद्ध पुरुष).

• In it he developed the famous "Drain of Wealth" theory, arguing that Britain was systematically draining India's wealth through home charges, salaries and pensions of British officials, and one-sided trade — thereby causing Indian poverty.

• Naoroji was also the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892, from Central Finsbury on a Liberal Party ticket).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the Indian National Congress three times — 1886 (Calcutta), 1893 (Lahore) and 1906 (Calcutta). At the 1906 session he declared "Swaraj" as the goal of the Congress.

• WC Bonnerji (Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee) — the first President of the Indian National Congress at its first session in Bombay, 1885.

• Pherozeshah Mehta — "the Lion of Bombay", Congress President in 1890.

• Badruddin Tyabji — the first Muslim President of the Congress, in 1887 (Madras).

NOTE

• Other economic-nationalist works: R.C. Dutt — "The Economic History of India"; M.G. Ranade — "Essays on Indian Economics"; G.V. Joshi and G. Subramania Iyer also wrote on the drain of wealth.

question: The efforts of Malayalam poet Vallathol Narayana Menon and dancer and guru Kalyanikutty Amma brought back and gave a new life to the dance form __________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mohiniyattam is the classical solo dance form of Kerala, performed traditionally by women. The name means "the dance of the enchantress (Mohini)".

• It had declined in the 19th century, and its revival in the 20th century was led by the Malayalam poet Vallathol Narayana Menon — who founded the Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) — and by the dancer-guru Kalyanikutty Amma, often called the "Mother of Mohiniyattam".

• Its style is lasya (graceful and gentle), with swaying body movements, white-and-gold kasavu costume, and lyrics usually in Manipravalam (a mix of Sanskrit and Malayalam).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.

• Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; traditionally a dance-drama, systematised by Siddhendra Yogi.

• Kathakali — Kerala; a vigorous tandava-oriented dance-drama with elaborate chutti make-up and masks, also nurtured at Kerala Kalamandalam.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Where was All Indian Muslim League formed in 1906?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhaka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka (Dacca), then in Eastern Bengal, at the end of the annual All India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

• Its founders included Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka, Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk; the first president was Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, the Aga Khan III.

• Its immediate objectives were to protect the political rights of Indian Muslims and to secure separate electorates, which were granted by the Indian Councils Act (Morley-Minto Reforms) of 1909.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Simla Deputation (1906), led by the Aga Khan, met Viceroy Lord Minto and demanded separate representation for Muslims — this directly preceded the League's formation.

• The Lucknow Pact of 1916 brought the Congress and the Muslim League together, with the Congress accepting separate electorates.

• The Lahore Resolution (1940), moved at the League's Lahore session by A.K. Fazlul Haq, is known as the "Pakistan Resolution".

NOTE

• Related foundations: Indian National Congress — 1885, Bombay (A.O. Hume); Hindu Mahasabha — 1915; Ghadar Party — 1913, San Francisco; Aligarh Movement/MAO College — 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

question: Which of the following writers wrote the autobiography ‘Truth, Love and a Little Malice’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khushwant Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Truth, Love and a Little Malice" (2002) is the autobiography of Khushwant Singh (1915–2014), the celebrated Indian novelist, journalist and columnist.

• He is best known for the Partition novel "Train to Pakistan" (1956), "I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale", "Delhi: A Novel", "The Company of Women" and the two-volume "A History of the Sikhs".

• He edited The Illustrated Weekly of India, The National Herald and The Hindustan Times, and wrote the long-running column "With Malice Towards One and All".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Khushwant Singh received the Padma Bhushan (1974) — which he returned in 1984 in protest against Operation Blue Star — and the Padma Vibhushan (2007).

• Chetan Bhagat — popular English fiction writer: Five Point Someone, 2 States, The 3 Mistakes of My Life.

• Pratibha Ray — Odia writer, Jnanpith Award (2011), famous for "Yajnaseni".

• Amrita Pritam — Punjabi poet and novelist, first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award (1956) and a Jnanpith (1981) laureate; her autobiography is "Rasidi Ticket" (Revenue Stamp) and her famous poem is "Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu".

NOTE

• Handy list of autobiographies: "My Experiments with Truth" — M.K. Gandhi; "An Autobiography / Toward Freedom" — Jawaharlal Nehru; "India Wins Freedom" — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; "Wings of Fire" — A.P.J. Abdul Kalam; "The Story of My Life" — Helen Keller.

question: In 2023, a three-day All-India Taekwondo Championship was organized in _________ to mark 50 years of Korea-India diplomatic relations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2023, a three-day All-India Taekwondo Championship was organised in New Delhi to commemorate 50 years of diplomatic relations between the Republic of Korea and India (established in 1973).

• The event was supported by the Korean Cultural Centre India and the Embassy of the Republic of Korea, and featured hundreds of participants from across the states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Taekwondo is a Korean martial art whose name means "the way of the foot and the fist". It became a full Olympic medal sport at the Sydney 2000 Games.

• Its world governing body is World Taekwondo, headquartered in Seoul; the national federation is the Taekwondo Federation of India.

• India-Korea ties were upgraded to a "Special Strategic Partnership" in 2015.

NOTE

• Other Korean-origin sports/martial arts in the exam syllabus: Judo, Karate (Japan), Kung-fu (China), Wushu (China), Sumo (Japan), Muay Thai (Thailand), Kalaripayattu (Kerala, India).

question: The outward remittances under the Reserve Bank of India’s ____________ made a strong comeback in the first quarter of FY23 as Indians increased spending on international travel, maintenance of close relatives and gifts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liberalised Remittance Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) of the Reserve Bank of India, all resident individuals, including minors, may freely remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year for any permissible current or capital account transaction.

• Permitted purposes include overseas travel, education, medical treatment, maintenance of close relatives, gifts and donations, and investment in shares/property abroad.

• The scheme was introduced in February 2004 (initially with a limit of USD 25,000) and the limit has been revised several times.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Remittances under LRS are subject to TCS (Tax Collected at Source) as per the Finance Act provisions; education and medical remittances enjoy concessional treatment.

• LRS does not permit remittance for margin trading, lottery, purchase of FCCBs, or transactions with countries identified as "non-cooperative" by the FATF.

• LRS is governed under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.

NOTE

• India has been the world's largest recipient of inward remittances for several years, crossing USD 100 billion in 2022 (World Bank).

• The other options — Regular Remittance Scheme, Liquid Remittances Scheme and Foreign Remittances Scheme — are not RBI schemes.

question: The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) scheme provide loans up to ________ to the non-corporate, non-farm small and micro entrepreneurs. (As of April 2023).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 lakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched on 8 April 2015. As of April 2023 it provided collateral-free institutional credit up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises.

• MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency Ltd., a refinancing institution set up as a subsidiary of SIDBI.

• Loans are given through banks, NBFCs, MFIs and RRBs in three categories:

◦ Shishu — up to ₹50,000

◦ Kishore — above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh

◦ Tarun — above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PMMY loans require no collateral security and carry no processing charges in most cases; a MUDRA card (a RuPay debit card) can be issued for working-capital needs.

• A large majority of PMMY accounts belong to women entrepreneurs, and a significant share to SC/ST/OBC borrowers.

NOTE

• Other credit-linked schemes: Stand Up India (₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs), PM SVANidhi (street vendors), PMEGP (Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme), CGTMSE (credit guarantee for micro and small enterprises).

question: What is the primary cause for the highest precipitation in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South-West Monsoon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The South-West Monsoon (June to September) brings about 75 per cent of India's total annual rainfall and is therefore the primary cause of the highest precipitation in the country.

• It sets in over Kerala around 1 June and withdraws by mid-September to early October. It has two branches — the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch.

• The monsoon is caused by the differential heating of land and sea, the northward shift of the ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone), the Tibetan Plateau heating and the Tropical Easterly Jet.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The North-East Monsoon (October–December), or the retreating monsoon, brings rain mainly to the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu, coastal Andhra Pradesh) — it is a regional, not the primary, rainfall source.

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra), both in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, record the highest rainfall in the world because of the funnel-shaped valleys of the Khasi Hills; but they are locations, not the cause of India's rainfall.

• The West Garo Hills also lie in Meghalaya and receive heavy orographic rain.

NOTE

• Rainfall types: orographic/relief (Western Ghats, Meghalaya), convectional (equatorial, "Mango showers" of Kerala/Karnataka), cyclonic/frontal (Western Disturbances bring winter rain to north-west India).

• Rain-shadow areas of India: eastern slopes of the Western Ghats — Pune, Solapur; Ladakh — a cold desert.

question: The ____________ maestros who revived the art form in the late 1940s include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Odissi is the classical dance form of Odisha, and its revival in the late 1940s was led by maestros such as Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, Guru Pankaj Charan Das, Guru Deba Prasad Das and Raghunath Dutta.

• Odissi is said to be the oldest surviving classical dance form of India, with evidence from the Ranigumpha caves of Udayagiri (2nd century BCE) and the sculptures of the Konark Sun Temple.

• Its characteristic features are the tribhanga (three-bend) posture and the chowk (square) stance, and its themes are largely drawn from Jayadeva's Gita Govinda and the worship of Lord Jagannath.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004) was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (2000); his famous disciples include Sanjukta Panigrahi, Sonal Mansingh, Madhavi Mudgal and Protima Bedi (founder of Nrityagram).

• Sattriya — Assam, created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardeva in the 15th century; recognised as classical in 2000.

• Manipuri — Manipur, centred on the Raas Leela of Radha-Krishna.

• Chhau — a semi-classical/folk martial dance of Odisha (Mayurbhanj), Jharkhand (Seraikella) and West Bengal (Purulia); inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

NOTE

• The Mahari (temple dancers) and Gotipua (young boys dressed as girls) traditions are the two roots from which modern Odissi grew.

question: The Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award 2022 was conferred upon Guru Niranjan Rout and Guru Ramahari Das for their contribution to the fields of ____________ dance and music.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award is instituted in memory of the legendary Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and is conferred for outstanding contribution to Odissi dance and music.

• The 2022 award was conferred upon Guru Niranjan Rout (Odissi dance) and Guru Ramahari Das (Odissi music).

• Both are eminent exponents from Odisha, and Guru Ramahari Das is a well-known Odissi vocalist and Padma Shri awardee.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra himself received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1966), Padma Shri (1972), Padma Bhushan (1988) and Padma Vibhushan (2000).

• Sattriya — Assam; Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Kathak — north India (the only classical form with strong Hindustani/Persian influence, known for tatkar footwork and chakkars).

NOTE

• Major dance awards and institutions: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (national academy for music, dance and drama, established 1952), Kalidas Samman (Madhya Pradesh), Kerala Kalamandalam (Vallathol Narayana Menon, 1930), Nrityagram (Protima Bedi, Bengaluru).

question: Which of the following is true about disposable income in relation to personal income?
option_1: Disposable income is equal to personal income.
option_2: Disposable income is always less than personal income.
option_3: Disposable income is always greater than personal income.
option_4: Disposable income can be greater or less than personal income, depending on taxes and deductions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Disposable income is always less than personal income.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Personal Income (PI) is the total income actually received by individuals and households from all sources before paying direct taxes.

• Disposable Personal Income (DPI) is the income left with households to spend or save after paying direct (personal) taxes and other compulsory payments (fines, fees, penalties).

◦ Formula: Disposable Income = Personal Income − Direct/Personal Taxes − Miscellaneous receipts of the government

• Since direct taxes can never be negative, DPI is always less than PI (at most equal, only in the hypothetical case of zero taxes). Hence Option 2 is the correct statement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chain of national income aggregates:

◦ NNP at factor cost = National Income (NI)

◦ PI = NI − Undistributed corporate profits − Corporate tax − Net interest paid by households + Transfer payments

◦ DPI = PI − Direct taxes − Miscellaneous receipts

◦ DPI = Consumption (C) + Saving (S)

• Only DPI, not PI, determines actual consumption and saving behaviour, which is why it is central to Keynesian consumption analysis.

NOTE

• Related terms: GDP (Gross Domestic Product), GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad, NNP = GNP − Depreciation, Per capita income = National income ÷ Population. In India these estimates are compiled by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI.

question: Which of the following best describes the process of calorimetry?
option_1: Measuring the amount of compressive strength
option_4: Measuring the amount of heat energy transferred
solution_text:
The correct answer is Measuring the amount of heat energy transferred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Calorimetry is the branch of science that deals with the measurement of the quantity of heat energy transferred during a physical change or a chemical reaction. The instrument used is a calorimeter.

• It is based on the Principle of Calorimetry (Law of Mixtures): when two bodies at different temperatures are mixed, heat lost by the hotter body = heat gained by the colder body, provided no heat escapes to the surroundings.

• The basic relation is Q = m × c × ΔT, where Q = heat, m = mass, c = specific heat capacity and ΔT = change in temperature.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (compressive strength) is measured by a Universal Testing Machine / compression testing machine.

• Option 2 (force) is measured by a dynamometer or spring balance; the SI unit is the newton (N).

• Option 3 (electricity) is measured by an ammeter (current), voltmeter (potential difference) or energy meter (electrical energy).

NOTE

• SI unit of heat is the joule (J); the older unit is the calorie (1 cal = 4.186 J).

• Specific heat capacity of water = 4186 J/kg/K, the highest among common liquids, which is why water is used as a coolant.

• Latent heat: fusion of ice = 3.34 × 10⁵ J/kg; vaporisation of water = 22.6 × 10⁵ J/kg.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 45.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 45 of the Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy (Part IV), now reads: "The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years."

• This present form was given by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, which also:

◦ inserted Article 21A — Right to free and compulsory education for children of 6–14 years as a Fundamental Right, and

◦ inserted Article 51A(k) — the fundamental duty of a parent/guardian to provide education to his child between 6 and 14 years.

• Before 2002, Article 45 asked the State to provide free and compulsory education for all children up to 14 years within ten years of the commencement of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 38 — the State shall secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people and minimise inequalities of income, status and opportunity.

• Article 39 — certain principles of policy: adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of material resources, equal pay for equal work [39(d)], protection of children and youth [39(e), 39(f)].

• Article 40 — organisation of Village Panchayats as units of self-government (basis of the 73rd Amendment, 1992).

NOTE

• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act came into force on 1 April 2010.

• Directive Principles are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) and are non-justiciable, inspired by the Irish Constitution.

question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body — it is an executive (non-statutory) body created by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission (itself set up by a Cabinet resolution in 1950).

• Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister; it has a Vice-Chairperson, a CEO, full-time and ex-officio members, and a Governing Council comprising the Chief Ministers of all States and Lieutenant Governors of UTs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Election Commission of India — Article 324; a constitutional body, set up on 25 January 1950 (celebrated as National Voters' Day).

• Finance Commission — Article 280; constituted by the President every five years to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States. The 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N.K. Singh.

• Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) — Articles 315 to 323; the central recruiting agency.

NOTE

• Other constitutional bodies: CAG (Art. 148), Attorney General (Art. 76), Advocate General (Art. 165), National Commission for SCs (Art. 338), STs (Art. 338A), Backward Classes (Art. 338B), Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Art. 350B), GST Council (Art. 279A).

• Statutory bodies (created by an Act of Parliament): NHRC, CVC, CIC, Lokpal, SEBI, UIDAI, NGT.

question: Which nutritional disorder is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin B1, which leads to problems of the peripheral nerves and wasting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beriberi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine). It damages the peripheral nerves and leads to wasting of the muscles.

◦ Dry beriberi — affects the nervous system: numbness, tingling, muscle weakness and wasting of limbs.

◦ Wet beriberi — affects the cardiovascular system: swelling (oedema), rapid heartbeat and heart failure.

• Rich sources of thiamine: whole grains, unpolished rice, pulses, nuts, yeast, pork and liver. Eating highly polished rice is a classic cause of beriberi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Xerophthalmia (dryness of the cornea, leading to night blindness and even total blindness) is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin A (Retinol).

• Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin) — usually due to a lack of "intrinsic factor" that helps its absorption.

• Rickets (soft, bent bones in children; osteomalacia in adults) is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D (Calciferol).

NOTE

• Other deficiency diseases: B2 (Riboflavin) → cheilosis/cracks at the corners of the mouth; B3 (Niacin) → pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia); B9 (Folic acid) → megaloblastic anaemia and neural tube defects; C (Ascorbic acid) → scurvy; K (Phylloquinone) → delayed blood clotting.

• Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C. Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E and K.

question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index of NITI Aayog 2021, which of the following states has less than 1% multidimensionally Poor of its total population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In NITI Aayog's first National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, released in November 2021 (based on NFHS-4, 2015-16 data), Kerala recorded the lowest incidence of multidimensional poverty in the country — only about 0.71 per cent of its population, i.e. less than 1 per cent.

• The index was developed in partnership with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the UNDP, following the global MPI (Alkire-Foster) methodology.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National MPI uses 3 dimensions and 12 indicators:

◦ Health — nutrition, child and adolescent mortality, maternal health

◦ Education — years of schooling, school attendance

◦ Standard of living — cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, bank account

• In that report the worst-performing states were Bihar (51.91%), Jharkhand (42.16%) and Uttar Pradesh (37.79%); among UTs, Puducherry was the best performer.

• In the second National MPI report (July 2023), based on NFHS-5 (2019-21), national multidimensional poverty fell from 24.85% (2015-16) to 14.96% (2019-21).

NOTE

• Kerala also leads on the Human Development Index, literacy rate and sex ratio among Indian states.

• Multidimensional poverty differs from income poverty, which uses a monetary poverty line (e.g. the Tendulkar and Rangarajan committee lines in India).

question: According to the Hindu calendar, Holi is celebrated on _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phalguna Purnima.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Holi, the festival of colours, is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) of the month of Phalguna, the last month of the Hindu lunar calendar. It usually falls in February–March.

• The night before is Holika Dahan (Chhoti Holi), when a bonfire commemorates the burning of Holika and the saving of Prahlada, the devotee of Lord Vishnu — symbolising the victory of good over evil.

• The next day, Rangwali Holi / Dhulandi, is played with colours (gulal) and water.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chaitra Purnima — Hanuman Jayanti; Chaitra Shukla Pratipada marks the beginning of the Hindu new year (Gudi Padwa / Ugadi).

• Pausa Purnima — Shakambhari Purnima; the month of Pausa also has Makar Sankranti.

• Magha Purnima — Maghi Purnima, an important bathing day at Prayagraj during the Magh Mela / Kumbh.

NOTE

• Regional forms of Holi: Lathmar Holi (Barsana and Nandgaon, UP), Basanta Utsav (Shantiniketan, West Bengal), Shigmo (Goa), Yaosang (Manipur), Hola Mohalla (Anandpur Sahib, Punjab — Sikh martial festival), Dol Jatra / Dol Purnima (Bengal and Odisha).

• The 12 months of the Hindu calendar: Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashwina, Kartika, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha, Phalguna.

question: Who was the music director of the famous song “Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon” sung by Lata Mangeshkar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C Ramchandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The patriotic song "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon" was composed (music directed) by C. Ramchandra (Chitalkar Ramchandra) and written by the poet Pradeep (Kavi Pradeep).

• It was sung by Lata Mangeshkar and first performed on 27 January 1963 at the National Stadium, New Delhi, in the presence of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.

• The song was a tribute to the soldiers who died in the India-China war of 1962, and it is said to have moved Nehru to tears.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kavi Pradeep (Ramchandra Narayanji Dwivedi) received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1997; he also wrote "Door hato ae duniya walon" from the film Kismet (1943).

• Kishore Kumar was a legendary playback singer, actor and occasional music director (e.g. Door Ka Rahi), not the composer of this song.

• Rajesh Roshan (son of composer Roshan) and Anand Raaj Anand are much later Bollywood music directors.

NOTE

• Other famous patriotic songs: "Vande Mataram" (Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, from Anandamath), "Sare Jahan Se Achha" (Muhammad Iqbal), "Jana Gana Mana" (Rabindranath Tagore — the National Anthem, adopted 24 January 1950), "Jhanda Ooncha Rahe Hamara" (Shyamlal Gupta 'Parshad').

question: In India, wild asses and camels are found in which type of forests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thorn forests and scrubs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tropical thorn forests and scrubs occur in regions receiving less than 70 cm of annual rainfall — north-western India, i.e. Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, parts of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

• The typical fauna of these dry regions includes wild ass, camel, rats, mice, rabbits, fox, wolf, tiger, lion and horses.

• Typical flora: Acacia (babool/kikar), palms, euphorbias, cacti, khair, neem, khejri and date palm; the plants have long roots and thick, fleshy stems with leaves reduced to spines to conserve water.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Indian Wild Ass (Ghudkhur / Equus hemionus khur) is found in the Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, protected in the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary (Wild Ass Sanctuary, Dhrangadhra).

• Tropical evergreen forests — rainfall above 200 cm: Western Ghats, Andaman and Nicobar, north-eastern hills; fauna includes elephants, monkeys, lemurs and deer.

• Montane forests — Himalayan slopes; fauna includes the Kashmir stag (Hangul), snow leopard, red panda, yak and Tibetan antelope.

• Mangrove/tidal forests — deltas of the Ganga-Brahmaputra (Sundarbans), Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna; famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger and Sundari trees.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian forests (as per NCERT): Tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen, Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests, Tropical thorn forests and scrubs, Montane forests, Mangrove (littoral and swamp) forests.

question: Which Indian sprinter bagged two gold medals, one each in the men's 100 and 200-metre races at the Flanders Cup 2023 athletics meet?

question: Who became the first Indian javelin ace to win the gold at the Zurich Diamond League?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian ever to win a Diamond League title when he won the javelin throw gold at the Zurich Diamond League Final in September 2022 with a throw of 88.44 m.

• He is India's first Olympic gold medallist in athletics, winning the javelin throw at the Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021) with a throw of 87.58 m.

• He also won the World Athletics Championships gold at Budapest in 2023 (88.17 m), becoming the first Indian world champion in athletics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Neeraj Chopra's other honours: Asian Games gold (2018 Jakarta, 2023 Hangzhou), Commonwealth Games gold (2018 Gold Coast), World U-20 Championship gold (2016 Bydgoszcz), and the Param Vishisht Seva Medal, Khel Ratna (2021) and Padma Shri (2022).

• His personal best is 89.94 m (Stockholm Diamond League, 2022).

• Sahil Silwal, Shivpal Yadav and Rohit Yadav are other Indian javelin throwers who have represented the country internationally but have not won a Diamond League title.

NOTE

• The Diamond League is the annual series of elite one-day track and field meetings organised by World Athletics, started in 2010.

question: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phillips curve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Phillips curve, given by the New Zealand-born economist A.W. Phillips in 1958, shows the inverse (negative) relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of change of money wages (and, by extension, the rate of inflation).

• In simple words: when unemployment is low, wages and prices rise faster; when unemployment is high, wage inflation slows down.

• The short-run Phillips curve is downward sloping, implying a trade-off between inflation and unemployment; the long-run Phillips curve is a vertical line at the natural rate of unemployment (the Friedman-Phelps critique).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Indifference curve — shows the different combinations of two goods that give a consumer the same level of satisfaction (utility); it is convex to the origin and slopes downward, with the slope being the Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS).

• Supply curve — shows the direct relationship between price and quantity supplied; it slopes upward.

• Demand curve — shows the inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded; it slopes downward (Law of Demand).

NOTE

• Other important curves in economics: Lorenz curve (income inequality, along with the Gini coefficient), Laffer curve (tax rate vs tax revenue), Engel curve (income vs consumption), Kuznets curve (growth vs inequality), Production Possibility Curve (PPC).

• Stagflation — the simultaneous occurrence of high inflation and high unemployment (as in the 1970s) — was the phenomenon that challenged the original Phillips curve.
